notes: Deep-agent RUN LIMITS (llm_agents/deep_agents/limits.py::run_limits) — how many and how large the LLM requests of one run may be. max_conversation_steps: the per-conversation hop budget the bridge/server defaults to (one LLM turn may call tools; the budget bounds turns). min_conversation_steps / max_steps_cap: the execute-node clamp on whatever a run asked for (a delegated fork gets +8 headroom under the same cap). recursion_limit: the LangGraph superstep bound for one graph invocation (plan + hops + replans + finalize + result). run_timeout_sec: the run's TOTAL wall-clock budget — the step lane checks it every hop and routes to finalize at the budget (the bridge's and the browser client's deadlines sit at the same value). llm_request_timeout_sec: the per-LLM-request wall-clock budget — the provider transport's retry ladder terminates at the budget (each attempt's read timeout shrinks to the remainder; the per-attempt read cap is the transport's 120s, so a larger budget buys MORE FRESH ATTEMPTS — the rescue for the provider's intermittent single-request hangs, 2026-11-03: two runs lost review-wave requests at 300s ≈ 2 attempts, raised to 600s ≈ 5); an overrun means the input is too heavy for one call and the caller refactors it into smaller tasks (the planner's slimmed init; the fork pre-planner's small call), never a same-payload retry. The budget bounds ONE individual LLM request (one chat completion, retries included) — NOT a graph node: a node (one step conversation hop) makes many such requests across its tool turns and legitimately outlasts this budget many times over; nodes are bounded by max_conversation_steps and the run by run_timeout_sec instead. max_plan_nodes / max_delegated_steps: the planned plan's step count and how many of those may be delegated forks. plan_repair_rounds: the planning session's propose-to-correct rounds per batch. plan_proposal_batches: the batched proposal protocol's round cap — the first call proposes the first few steps, every later round proposes the next batch over the nodes-so-far (each a small LLM call that persists immediately; the plan closes when the model replies more:false), so planning never hangs on one giant reply. max_total_plan_steps / max_fork_children: the replan guards (update_plan total nodes, forks per node). max_parallel_delegated_steps: the fork-wave width per hop (the parallel wave is LangGraph's parallel-join semantics: consecutive delegated-or-parallel steps run concurrently and the NEXT merge node — the first unmarked inline step, normally the custom graph's synthesis step — starts only after EVERY member settles, failed members included). max_concurrent_subagents: the per-agent spawn semaphore. max_spawn_depth: spawn-chain depth (an agent at the depth carries no spawn tool). subagent_timeout_sec: wall clock per spawned child, null = unbounded. max_output_tokens: the per-LLM-request output ceiling (the runaway guard). max_output_repairs: output-validation repair rounds per conversation. finding_max_chars / findings_block_max_chars: the findings bridge's per-finding and whole-block caps (older findings age to title lines past the block cap). prompt_eager_rows / prompt_eager_chars: the eager skill-loading budget before the planner's verdict decides. prompt_hotpath_rows / hotpath_probe_chains: the KG-HOTPATH corroboration lane (planning/kg_prompts.py, 2026-11-07) — optional-labeled skills the PROMOTED llm.kg_hotpaths chains implicate (the run's question trigram-matches a promoted query; the chain's ns1 entities name the skill or its optional labels hit the chain's bilingual entity vocabulary) auto-load at plan time, at most prompt_hotpath_rows rows per run (0 disables the lane — bound-label rows always load regardless), probing at most hotpath_probe_chains top-hit_count chains. payload_guard_chars / payload_entry_max_chars / payload_preview_chars / payload_preview_items: the LARGE-PAYLOAD PRE-CHECK (llm_agents/deep_agents/payload_guard.py) at every message builder — a structured-context subtree whose serialized size passes payload_entry_max_chars ships as _guarded metadata + preview (payload_preview_chars per value, payload_preview_items per container) with a prompt block naming what was elided so the model re-fetches and checks the real data through its tools; payload_guard_chars is the whole-block gate that trims the largest remaining top-level entries down to it. tool_result_max_chars: the head+tail cap on ONE tool result's text before it enters the conversation transcript. Takes effect on the NEXT run — the daemon re-reads per run, no restart needed. supervisor_poll_interval_sec / supervisor_repair_grace_sec / supervisor_max_node_retries / supervisor_max_repairs_per_run: the SUPERVISOR REPAIR LANE (2026-11-06) — the per-run backend poller watches node states while the graph runs; on a root-path step failure the step lane opens a bounded pause window (the grace) for the supervisor agent's verdict, and a transient error (rate limit, timeout, upstream 5xx) within both retry budgets gets its failed row re-opened and the hop re-run. grace 0 disables repair (the lane never waits); healthy runs pay one cheap DB poll per interval and zero LLM. supervisor_retry_throttle_sec: the cooldown a rate-limit-class retry waits INSIDE the repair pause window before the hop re-runs (2026-11-06: immediate re-runs re-hit the account rate limit; grace 120 covers intervention + 45).
